newsitem.title: UK: Coffee group in maiden talks with industry leaders.
newsitem.headline: Coffee group in maiden talks with industry leaders.

text.p: The International Coffee Organization (ICO) on Wednesday held informal talks with several coffee trade leaders to help lay the ground for future dialogue on key issues affecting the coffee sector.

The gathering, held in the sidelines of the week-long ICO meetings, took place hours after key producing nations decided to extend their current cartel-style quotas for 12 more months in a move to lock in gains from this year's spectacular rally.
New York arabica coffee futures rose 10 cents to top $2.50 per pound after news of the London accord by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC).

Although the ICO gathering did not specifically discuss the ACPC decision and coffee prices, the trade leaders were certainly concerned with the impact of the persistently high bean prices on consumer demand.

"There were no coffeee discussions per se at all -- simply a meeting to see is there a way to organize a vehicle for the private sector to communicate. And ICO simply provided the vehicle for that first meeting," said Robert Nelson, president of the National Coffee Association of U.S.
He told Reuters after the meeting that there could a consumer backlash in the U.S. at some point if the prices continue to spiral.
"Coffee is obviously a very good value, but I can tell you there certainly is concern with any product with pricing and that United States consumers are sensitive to pricing," he said.
"So, it is something that one is certainly conscious of -- be it coffee or be it clothing. And there is a certain point the consumers, regardless of the product, will react to pricing."

When asked whether coffee prices were at a level which consumers would start to turn away from coffee, he said "It's difficult to say only because I've not done the research necessary really to determine where those price points are."
"However, overall, pricing of any consumer product is something consumers are sensitive of but just where that point is is really difficult for me to say."
Folgers and some other major U.S. coffee roasters have put up their retail prices a few times this year as they responded to the steep increase in bean prices.
Among those who attended the ICO talks include trade representatives from Europe, Latin America and Indonesia. --Medora Lee, Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
